documents.unit: Student Handbook / Honor Code (Educational Policy Committee statement on AI)
documents.title: The Honor Code (incl. EPC Policy Statement on AI and Generative AI Statements)
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); AI provision in force since Fall 2023
documents.summary: The Honor Code page carries the faculty-passed EPC statement that AI in submitted coursework is an Honor Code violation unless an instructor permits it, and that permitted use must be acknowledged. It also reproduces the August 2024 Academic Affairs statement asking instructors to set course-level AI expectations and to tell students about detection tools.
documents.stance_why: The EPC statement says "Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor, the use of artificial intelligence ... is a violation of the Honor Code", so AI is banned by default and allowed only where the instructor permits it, which is restrict. The longer statement leaves details to instructors but does not change that default.

documents.title: Generative AI Statements
documents.summary: The Center for Faculty Career Development page repeats the EPC rule that unpermitted AI use is an Honor Code violation, then gives instructors practical guidance: state expectations in each syllabus, align AI use with learning goals, do not rely only on detectors, talk to the student first, and protect student data. It offers a spectrum from maximally restrictive to maximally encouraging policies.
documents.stance_why: The page opens with "Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor, the use of artificial intelligence ... is a violation of the Honor Code", a default ban lifted only by instructor permission, so restrict. The guidance after it asks instructors to choose between maximally restrictive and maximally encouraging policies, but it does not set tiers itself.

documents.title: Wesleyan University Generative AI Usage Policy
documents.summary: The ITS policy allows generative AI use by faculty, staff and students on condition that data classification rules are followed, tools are reviewed and approved by ITS, and users verify output. It is mostly about data protection and procurement, with brief mentions of academic integrity and copyright.
documents.stance_why: The policy states the university "aims to balance the innovative potential of generative AI" with data protection and lists which tools may take which data classes; AI use is allowed with conditions, which is permit. It sets no rule on coursework AI use and refers to the Honor Code for that.

units.why: The Purpose states the university "aims to balance the innovative potential of generative AI (AI) with the need to protect sensitive information, uphold academic integrity", setting the purpose and principles of the policy (P56).
units.anchor: aims to balance the innovative potential of generative AI

units.why: "This policy is not exhaustive, but represents work towards a thorough and comprehensive policy" admits the policy is provisional (P54).
units.anchor: This policy is not exhaustive, but represents work towards a thorough and comprehensive policy.

units.why: The scope "applies to all faculty, staff, students, and affiliates" who put university information in AI tools; this sets what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: This policy applies to all faculty, staff, students, and affiliates

units.why: "Users must comply with all relevant Wesleyan University policies, as well as applicable state and federal laws" including integrity, copyright and data classification, which is P77.
units.anchor: Users must comply with all relevant Wesleyan University policies

units.why: "Only information classified as "Public" may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools" protects data by class, which is P50.
units.anchor: Only information classified as "Public" may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools

units.why: "If the tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as 'Sensitive'" prefers vetted tools for sensitive data, P50.
units.anchor: reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as "Sensitive"
units.policy: Information classified as Sensitive may be entered only into a generative AI tool that has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS.

units.why: "cannot be entered into any generative AI tool without explicit written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and the relevant Cabinet member" names who grants exceptions (P80).
units.anchor: without explicit written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer
units.fit_note: Mainly a data rule; classed here for the named approvers and exception route.

units.why: "It is the user's responsibility to review the terms and conditions" puts the risk of tool terms on users (P114); partial since it concerns research data compliance.
units.anchor: It is the user's responsibility to review the terms and conditions
units.fit_note: Concerns checking terms and data ingestion for research data, not liability for signing up to a tool.

units.why: "users must consult with the university's ITS department to ensure these tools undergo a thorough risk assessment" requires institutional review before getting AI tools, P65.
units.anchor: users must consult with the university's ITS department

units.why: "follow the procurement procedures as outlined in the Vendor Management Policy" sets how to request licenses, adding to the review rule; P65 covers review and approval of tools before purchase.
units.anchor: follow the procurement procedures as outlined in the Vendor Management Policy

units.why: "AI Generated content may be misleading, fabricated, or false" and users must verify it, which is P31.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for verifying the accuracy of content generated by AI tools

units.why: "ensuring that it does not infringe on copyright" makes users responsible for copyright in AI output, P52.
units.anchor: ensuring that it does not infringe on copyright

units.why: The Appendix lists tools allowed for Sensitive Data, including "Microsoft Copilot (Wesleyan license only)", naming the approved licensed tools (P92).
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot
units.policy: Sensitive Data can be used only in ChatGPT Enterprise and Business, Claude Team and Enterprise, Zoom AI Companion, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini (Wesleyan license only).

units.why: "Restricted Data cannot be used by any generative AI tools without prior approval", with FERPA, SSNs and PHI as examples, protects personal data (P50).
units.anchor: Restricted Data cannot be used by any generative AI tools without prior approval

notes: Honor Code page repeats the EPC statement and the Aug 2024 statement; the rest of the Honor Code (plagiarism guide, hearing process, pledges) was read but is not AI-specific except the plagiarism line. The CFCD page repeats the same material and adds an extended guidance list. Course-layer documents were deferred in the collect file.
